rule Suspicious_Rundll32_From_Temp {
    meta:
        description = "Detects rundll32.exe loading DLLs from temp directories"
        author = "SOC Team"
        maltype = "T1055, T1218.011"
    strings:
        $s1 = "\\Temp\\" nocase
        $s2 = "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" nocase
        $s3 = "rundll32.exe" nocase
    condition:
        $s3 and ($s1 or $s2)
}

rule CobaltStrike_Shellcode_Rundll32 {
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory patterns associated with Cobalt Strike shellcode injection via rundll32"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        maltype = "RAT"
        severity = 1
    strings:
        $a = { 6A 40 68 00 30 00 00 6A 14 8D 91 }
        $b = { B8 90 01 00 00 BA 90 01 00 00 E8 } in (codepage)
        $c = "ReflectiveLoader" fullword ascii
    condition:
        all of them
}

arguments.summary: Initial low-severity port scan alert escalated to critical incident following correlation with historical IDS alerts, EDR telemetry, and SIEM data. The source IP 10.0.5.14 was misidentified in initial logs; true source is 10.0.5.42 (WS-FIN-042), a high-criticality finance workstation. Host exhibits clear indicators of compromise: Cobalt Strike beaconing (T1071.001), encoded PowerShell execution (T1566.001), unsigned DLL loading via rundll32 (T1218.011), and lateral movement attempts via SMB. Despite a sandbox verdict of 'clean' for a submitted file, behavioral telemetry and network activity confirm malicious activity. No containment actions were executed due to incorrect source attribution in the initial alert.
